question.text: Mr. Ramesh currently spends Rs. 45,000 per month on household expenses. He expects to retire in 25 years. If inflation averages 6% per annum, what will his monthly expenses be at the time of retirement (approximate value)?

explanation.text: The Logic: Future value of current expenses = Rs. 45,000 x (1.06)^25. (1.06)^25 ≈ 4.29187. Therefore Rs. 45,000 x 4.29187 ≈ Rs. 1,93,134, applying the standard compound-growth formula FV = PV x (1+r)^n. The Trap: Rs. 1,12,500 results from multiplying Rs. 45,000 by 2.5 (a rough mental estimate that ignores compounding); Rs. 1,57,826 reflects a lower inflation rate or fewer years; Rs. 2,58,227 reflects using 7% instead of 6%. Note: The answer is the closest approximation to Rs. 45,000 x (1.06)^25; small differences from exact compounding depend on rounding of (1.06)^25.
